title: Console analytics request eligibility matrix and export data contract
creator: Priya Nair
description: Goal: Create a deterministic eligibility matrix and data contract for console analytics and exports so enterprise requests (usage analytics, granular cost breakdowns, scheduled exports, customer-facing dashboards) can be triaged and routed to the correct delivery lane (self-serve, Product Ops, Professional Services). Scope: 1) Define request attributes (data scope, retention, row-level sensitivity, freshness SLA, aggregation level, cadence) and map them to eligibility lanes. 2) Create a canonical export data contract (fields, schemas, required identifiers, de-identification rules) for common console exports (workspace usage, token-level cost, model route traces). 3) Produce a routing matrix and scoring rubric for prioritization that can be evaluated automatically at intake or surfaced to a PM reviewer. Non-goals: replacing existing billing system or building the export runner; engineering tickets will be created for implementation-specific schemas and APIs.
decision_log: 2026-02-15 Priya Nair: Opted to prefer a small set of canonical schemas rather than ad-hoc per-customer CSVs to reduce long-term maintenance overhead.
2026-02-22 Marco Chen: Chose three priority lanes (Self-serve SDK, Console scheduled export, PS-assisted delivery) based on required data sensitivity and SLA.
2026-03-03 Eng sync: Agreed to enforce row-level sensitive flags at the contract level and require SSO/KMS for exports marked as 'sensitive'.
tradeoffs: Granularity vs latency: very fine-grained event streams increase cost and storage — we will default to daily aggregated exports and offer hourly for P0 enterprise contracts.
Flexibility vs maintainability: standardized schemas limit ad-hoc requests but significantly reduce custom engineering per-customer.
Automation vs human review: scoring rubric automates ~70% of triage; the remainder will route to PM/solutions for contextual judgment.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical JSON Schema for the three export types (usage_summary, token_costs_by_route, workspace_traces) published in Confluence.
A documented eligibility matrix with clear thresholds (row-level sensitivity, retention > 90 days, SLA <= 24h, cost-allocation tags present) and routing outcome for each cell.
An intake webhook prototype that returns a triage_result (lane, score, required follow-ups) for sample customer requests.
Stakeholder sign-off from Sales engineering, Billing, Security, and PS recorded in ticket comments.
implementation_notes: Markup canonical schema names to include version (usage_summary.v1) to allow future evolution without breaking exports.
Add an enforcement flag 'requires_deid' for exports that need tokenization/de-identification pre-export; PS/Eng will own tooling.
Design intake form fields in Console: data_range, metrics_requested, aggregation_level, target_destination, retention, encryption_required.
Create stub API path /intake/analytics-triage to return JSON for the prototype; actual exports will be queued by a downstream jobs service.
